zh: 终态只有两种值：形状内全部为 a，背景全部为 b，且 a ≠ b；对固定的 (a, b)，需要修改的恰好是值不等于所属区域目标值的格子。
分别统计形状内和背景中 0、1、2 的个数；固定 (a, b) 时可以保留 inside[a] + outside[b] 个格子。有序且不同的值对只有六种，全部枚举取最小代价。
令 m = n/2，格子 (i, j) 属于形状当且仅当 i ≤ m 且 (j = i 或 j = n−1−i)，或 i ≥ m 且 j = m；扫描一遍统计 inside 和 outside（中心只算一次）；枚举 a ≠ b，答案为 n² 减去 inside[a] + outside[b] 的最大值。所有格子都相同时也必须把形状改成另一种值。
en: The final grid uses exactly two values: a everywhere in the shape and b everywhere in the background, with a ≠ b; for a fixed (a, b), the cells to change are exactly those whose value differs from their region's target.

Count the 0s, 1s, and 2s inside the shape and in the background separately; for a fixed (a, b), inside[a] + outside[b] cells can stay. There are only six ordered pairs of different values, so try them all and take the cheapest.

With m = n/2, cell (i, j) is on the shape exactly when i ≤ m and (j = i or j = n−1−i), or when i ≥ m and j = m; one scan fills inside and outside (the center counts once); over all a ≠ b the answer is n² minus the largest inside[a] + outside[b]. Even when every cell is equal, the shape must be changed to another value.

explanationEn:
## Original Koddi Coordinates, Ranges from the Same Problem, and Summary-Page Corrections

In the fixed commit e66f809f4c953bce129f68491726176615db6afc, OA LIST/Koddi_OA/004_image.txt defines the Y shape of the protein matrix: from the top-left and top-right along the diagonals to the center, then vertically from the center to the bottom. 005 confirms the coordinates by highlighting each cell; 006/007 give complete 3×3 and 5×5 inputs with outputs 2 and 8 respectively; 008 shows the 5×5 transformation again. The shape is one color, the background is one color, and the two colors differ, giving 6 color assignments in total.

KoddiOCR did not preserve the odd-order guarantee or numeric bounds on n. The cross-company evidence for the same problem: the complete 3×3 and 5×5 inputs of Koddi006 and OA LIST/Databricks_OA/021_image.txt match, as do both outputs 2/8, the two sets of changed positions, the complete target matrices, and the explanation of changing 8 zeros to 1; the highlighted positions of Koddi005 and Databricks020 match. Only the protein narrative and the variable names were changed; the match is not guessed from the title.

The ranges are adopted according to the evidence: Databricks019 states explicitly that n is odd; the same problem in fastprep/Databricks/databricks-write-l-matrix.md constrains 5≤n≤99 with elements 0..2, but the original example shared by all sources has n=3. The complete envelope is therefore the union of {3} and the odd numbers 5..99, i.e., the odd numbers 3..99. n=1 is not added; this site does not claim that Koddi or DatabricksOCR itself gives the upper bound 99. fastprep's L story and the Databricks title's X conflict with the explicit coordinates, so the coordinates take precedence. fastprep's second example is missing a row, but Koddi006/007 already have the complete 5×5, so no row needs to be guessed.

The Koddi summary page's cross matrix [[0,1,0],[1,1,1],[0,1,0]] claims an answer of 1, but enumerating the six final states gives a minimum of 4: the Y region has 2 each of 0/1, and the background has 3 ones and 2 zeros; making Y 0 and the background 1 changes 4 cells and reaches the lower bound. The summary page's "4n−2 Y cells" is also wrong; the correct count is (3n−1)/2. This site keeps the two original OCR examples 2/8 and does not reuse the wrong summary example. The third public example is added by this site. Upstream code was not executed.

## Coordinate definition and approach

Use 0-based coordinates and let m=n//2. The shape is the union of three segments: (t,t) and (t,n−1−t) with 0≤t≤m, and (t,m) with m≤t<n. The center is a single cell of the union and is counted only once. All cells in the shape must be the same value a; all background cells must be another value b with a≠b, where a and b are chosen from 0/1/2.

Count the frequencies of the three values inside and outside the shape separately, as inside and outside. If the target is (a,b), inside[a]+outside[b] cells can be kept and every other cell must be changed, at a cost of n²−inside[a]−outside[b]. Enumerate the six ordered pairs of different values and take the minimum cost.

## Proof of correctness

The coordinate predicate fully covers the two upper half-diagonals and the vertical line below the center; each cell is visited only once, the center is not counted twice, and the shape and background form a disjoint partition of all cells.

For fixed different target values a and b, a cell whose original value is already correct needs no change, while each cell whose original value differs from the target of its region must be changed at least once. One operation can change such a cell directly to the target value, so changing all wrong cells reaches exactly this lower bound. inside[a]+outside[b] is exactly the number of cells that can be kept, so the computed cost is the true minimum for that target. Any valid final state must correspond to one of the six ordered pairs of different values, and enumerating the six pairs covers every kind of final state without duplication or omission, so the minimum cost is globally optimal.

## Complexity and edge cases

Scanning the n² cells and enumerating the 6 color assignments takes O(n²) time, and the frequency counts need only O(1) extra space (storing the input takes O(n²)). For the full n=99 there are 9801 cells, and the shape has (3n−1)/2=148 cells. A matrix whose cells are all the same should change 148 cells, recoloring the shape to another value, rather than wrongly letting the shape and the background share a value and outputting 0. The answer does not exceed n², so ordinary integers suffice.

## Independent verification

163 unique oracles first build the shape set explicitly from the three coordinate segments, then construct the 6 complete target matrices and compute the Hamming distance cell by cell, without using the region-frequency formula. In addition, all 19683 three-valued 3×3 matrices were checked exhaustively against the original reference function, and input/expected digests were saved; this is an in-process check, while the 163 oracles and all official cases were additionally run as real subprocesses.

The official edge cases include full order-99 matrices of all 0, all 1, and all 2, all six perfect color assignments, errors at the center and at the bottom, X-shaped distractors, checkerboards, and random matrices. The order-99 data are still all verified by the independent target-matrix oracle, with additional closed-form checks for all-equal matrices, perfect shapes, and single-cell changes. Two wrong programs, one that allows both regions to share a value and one that wrongly takes the two full diagonals as the target, are each counted as killed only after exiting normally on all official data.
